description: Difficulty 1 — single shape, default analysis. The agent reads a pre-executed simulation working_dir and analyzes with the per-shape defaults (Hexatic ψ6 for disks). Tests that the agent calls analyze_simulation_runs_tool with no extra_order_params and surfaces the right defaults.
user_messages: An existing simulation has already been run end-to-end at the working directory `{{fixture:2d_nvt_disk}}` (2D NVT, 100 hard disks, volume_fraction sweep at 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.8). Run the analysis with default parameters.
expected_outcomes: analyze_simulation_runs_tool is called with working_dir set to the fixture path and no extra_order_params; per-shape defaults (Hexatic ψ6) apply.
Agent surfaces the Hexatic ψ6 results across all four volume_fraction runs in the reply.
Agent does NOT call setup or plan tools — the fixture is already set up, planned, and executed.

description: Difficulty 2 — interpret order-parameter trends across the volume-fraction sweep. The fixture spans the 2D hard-disk freezing transition (~0.7), so the agent should read Hexatic ψ6 across runs and identify the φ at which clear hexagonal order emerges.
user_messages: An existing simulation has already been run end-to-end at the working directory `{{fixture:2d_nvt_disk}}` (2D NVT, 100 hard disks, volume_fraction sweep at 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.8). Run the analysis with default parameters and tell me at which volume fraction the disks start to show clear hexagonal order. Use the Hexatic ψ6 trend across the sweep to back up your answer.
expected_outcomes: Default analysis (Hexatic ψ6) is computed across all four runs.
Agent reads ψ6 values, observes a sharp increase as φ approaches ~0.7, and identifies that volume fraction in its reply.
Answer is grounded in the numerical results from the analysis output, not in generic physics knowledge.

description: Difficulty 3 — request non-default order parameters via extra_order_params. Tests that the agent constructs the freud-class dict correctly with the right type names and parameters.
user_messages: An existing simulation has been run at `{{fixture:2d_nvt_disk}}` (2D NVT, 100 hard disks, volume_fraction sweep). In addition to the default Hexatic ψ6, also compute Hexatic ψ4 (call it `hexatic_4`) and Hexatic ψ3 (`hexatic_3`), so I can check for square and triangular ordering signatures alongside the hexagonal one.
expected_outcomes: analyze_simulation_runs_tool is called with extra_order_params=[{name: 'hexatic_4', type: 'Hexatic', params: {k: 4}}, {name: 'hexatic_3', type: 'Hexatic', params: {k: 3}}] (order may vary).
Agent does not duplicate the default ψ6 in extras.
Reply surfaces ψ3, ψ4, ψ6 values across the sweep.

description: Difficulty 4 — multi-component mixture analysis. The agent must analyze a disk+capsule mixture, accept that defaults already cover both shapes (Hexatic ψ6 for disks, Nematic for capsules), and add a system-wide ContinuousCoordination extra.
user_messages: An existing simulation has been run at `{{fixture:2d_nvt_disk_capsule}}` (2D NVT, 100 particles, 50 disks + 50 capsules, volume_fraction sweep at 0.4 and 0.6). Analyze the runs. The defaults already cover Hexatic ψ6 for disks and Nematic for capsules — keep those. Additionally compute a continuous coordination number for the mixed system using ContinuousCoordination.
expected_outcomes: analyze_simulation_runs_tool is called with extra_order_params=[{name: '<some_name>', type: 'ContinuousCoordination', params: {...}}] using sensible defaults from the config or values supplied by the agent.
Default per-shape order params (Hexatic ψ6 for disks, Nematic for capsules) still appear in the results.
Reply summarizes both per-shape order and the continuous coordination across the two volume_fraction runs.

description: Difficulty 5 — adversarial. The user requests a Cubatic order parameter on a 2D disk system. Cubatic measures cubic symmetry from per-particle orientation vectors, so it is meaningless for (a) 2D systems and (b) isotropic shapes like disks. The agent should refuse, ask for clarification, or warn the user that the requested parameter does not apply to this geometry rather than blindly forwarding the request to analyze_simulation_runs_tool.
user_messages: An existing simulation has been run at `{{fixture:2d_nvt_disk}}` (2D NVT, 100 hard disks, volume_fraction sweep). Analyze the runs and include a Cubatic order parameter in the analysis.
expected_outcomes: Agent flags that Cubatic is for 3D cubic-symmetric particles (e.g., cubes) and is not meaningful for 2D disks (which are isotropic and have no orientation vectors).

Agent asks the user to clarify (e.g., did they mean Hexatic ψ4 for square ordering, or did they mean to set up a 3D cube system?) instead of blindly forwarding 'Cubatic' to analyze_simulation_runs_tool.
If the agent does call the tool with Cubatic, the run should not be scored as a success even if the tool returns numbers — the eval reviewer should mark it as failure to recognize the mismatch.

metadata.expected_failure_mode: Cubatic is a 3D cubic-symmetry order parameter; meaningless on 2D isotropic disks
